title: Thu 5 Nov: Nifty's fifth straight gain as Democrats win Congress
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty rose for a fifth straight day to a two-month closing high as Democrats swept Congress, and GIFT Nifty points to a gap-up. Then: IT, the rupee, oil, US yields, Airtel, Titan, HDFC Bank, ONGC and Dabur.

1. Nifty gains for a fifth day to a two-month closing high of 23,961 as Democrats win Congress (Upstox; HDFC Sky; Kotak Neo)
2. IT stocks fall 1.5% as investors weigh what a Democratic Congress means for AI spending (Upstox; Yahoo Finance (Investopedia); TradingKey)
3. Rupee firms for a fourth day to 94.64 as the dollar slips after the US midterms (HDFC Sky; CappNotes; 5paisa)
4. Brent settles 8.7% lower at 94.62 dollars as the Democratic sweep trims the war premium (Rigzone (Bloomberg); Al Jazeera)
5. US 10-year Treasury yield falls about 6 bp to 4.89% as Democrats sweep Congress (CappNotes; Finwire; Seeking Alpha)
6. Bharti Airtel reports September-quarter results; brokerages expect 14-15% revenue growth and ARPU near 268 rupees (Business Standard)
7. Titan jumps 4.2% ahead of Dhanteras and its September-quarter results on 5 Nov (Upstox; Kotak Neo; Bloomingbit (Reuters))
8. HDFC Bank extends its run as foreign buying lifts private lenders (5paisa; Liquide; Yahoo Finance)
9. ONGC's board meets on 5 Nov for results and an interim dividend as Brent slides (PSU Connect; Rigzone (Bloomberg); Dimsum Daily)
10. Dabur's profit rises 12% to 506 crore rupees on 5.5% volume growth, but margins slip (Business Today)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm Pri.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm SU. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: a fifth straight gain for the Nifty, and a gap-up signal after Democrats swept Congress.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: SU, what happened on Wednesday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty closed at 23,960.60, up 0.63%, a two-month closing high. The Sensex rose 0.50% to 77,301.40. That's five gains in a row.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Small caps did even better, up about 2%, and 36 of the 50 Nifty stocks closed higher.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved the index?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: BEL was the top Nifty gainer, up 4.71%, and Adani Enterprises rose 4.47%. On the other side, TCS was the biggest loser, down 2.52%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And overnight? I hear Wall Street had a big night.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It did. The Dow jumped 3.03% and the S&P 500 rose 1.58%, as Brent fell 8.7%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: GIFT Nifty traded at 24,369.50, up 1.75%, at 2:41 am India time. That points to a gap-up open.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Why should India care who controls the US Congress?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. Traders read the Democratic sweep as fiscal gridlock and a faster end to the Iran war. That means cheaper oil, which India imports.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And foreign money is pouring in. FIIs bought a net 7,284 crore rupees of shares on Wednesday, after 6,837 crore on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's the trigger to watch today?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The 24,000 mark. A gap above it tests whether this five-day, foreign-buying rally can push past resistance. Profit-taking near 24,000 is the risk.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: BEL, Adani Enterprises and TCS. Sentiment: positive.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: IT was the only sector in the red. Why?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty IT fell 1.5%. TCS dropped 2.52% to 2,436 rupees, HCLTech fell 2.37% and Infosys 1.73%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Even though US Big Tech rallied?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Microsoft rose about 7%, but Nvidia fell about 3% and Micron more than 7% after Texas's incoming governor pledged a moratorium on new data-centre approvals.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: US policy on AI spending now moves Indian IT on its own. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: TCS, HCLTech, Infosys, Wipro.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: the rupee firms for a fourth day.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee settled at a provisional 94.58 per dollar, up 17 paise, according to PTI. Reuters put the close at 94.64.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Overnight the dollar index fell 0.34% to 101.53, and Brent's slide helps too.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who gains from a stronger rupee?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Airlines, whose fuel and dollar costs both fall. Exporters like TCS earn a little less in rupee terms.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: cheaper oil and foreign inflows ease pressure on India's import bill. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: IndiGo, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: oil's war premium is melting fast.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent for January settled at 94.62 dollars, down 8.7%, after touching 93.22, its lowest since 31 August. WTI fell 8.3% to 88.12 dollars.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What changed?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Traders bet a Democratic Congress speeds an end to the Iran war, and JPMorgan says the market is back in surplus. Iran still called the US reply unconvincing.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: oil near 95 dollars, not 115, cuts India's import bill and inflation. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: BPCL, IOC, IndiGo, Asian Paints.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: US bond yields drop. Why should I care?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The US 10-year yield closed about 6 basis points lower, near 4.89%. The 2-year fell about 5 basis points to 4.59%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Investors priced fiscal gridlock. December Fed-hike odds slipped to about 77%. Jobless claims come today, and payrolls on Friday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: lower US yields ease pressure on emerging-market currencies and support foreign flows into India. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Airtel reports today. What's the bar?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Kotak expects revenue of about 59,750 crore rupees, up 14.5%. Axis Direct expects 60,061 crore. ARPU is seen at 268 to 269 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The stock closed at 2,067.60 rupees, nearly flat, after a 3.8% run into results.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: it's the first big read on Indian telecom pricing since Jio's listing. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, Bharti Hexacom.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: Titan jumps just before Dhanteras.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Titan rose 4.22% to 4,754.40 rupees and reports today. Kotak Neo expects profit of 1,274 to 1,419 crore rupees, about 27% higher.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Does gold's big jump help?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Gold settled about 3.4% higher, near 4,073 dollars an ounce, its biggest daily gain since August. That lifts jewellers' inventory values.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Titan's jewellery growth is the main listed read on festive gold demand. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Lalithaa Jewellery.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: HDFC Bank keeps running.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: HDFC Bank rose 1.54% to 736.70 rupees, about 5% in two days. Nifty Bank gained 0.67% to 55,913.60.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Is that run getting stretched?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit-taking after a 5% two-day run is the risk. But foreign buying has concentrated in the largest private bank.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: HDFC Bank is the biggest single channel for foreign money into Indian shares. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: ONGC reports today, in a rough week for oil producers.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: ONGC closed at 235 rupees, up 1.2%, before today's board meeting on results and an interim dividend.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Overnight, energy was the worst S&P sector, down 4.74%, with ExxonMobil off 5.3%. PetroChina fell more than 5% in Hong Kong.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: ONGC's realisations move almost one for one with Brent. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: ONGC, Oil India.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: Dabur's numbers are out.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit rose 11.7% to 505.5 crore rupees and revenue 11.6% to 3,563 crore. India FMCG volumes grew 5.5%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any catch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Operating margin fell 60 basis points. Dabur declared an interim dividend of 3.50 rupees. The stock had already risen 3.45% to 394.10 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Dabur's volumes show whether rural and festive demand is holding up. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Dabur, Godrej Consumer.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: whether the Nifty opens above 24,000, results from Airtel, Titan and ONGC, and the Bank of England decision.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
